title: “The” goes on the end: kaffen, huset
objective: Make a noun definite by adding -en or -et.
explanation: Danish puts “the” at the end of the noun. An en-word adds -en: “en kop” → “koppen”, “en bil” → “bilen”. An et-word adds -et: “et hus” → “huset”, “et glas” → “glasset”. Short words with a short vowel often double the last consonant (glas → glasset, kop → koppen). This is why learning en or et first pays off.
sourceReference: Deepwater original starter course (2026-10-29), written for Echo; teacher review required before publishing.

exercises.feedbackIncorrect: Bil is an en-word, so “the car” is “bilen”.
Kaffe ends in -e, so just add -n: “kaffen”.

exercises.prompt: Take two of your en/et words from the last lesson and write a short sentence with each in the “the” form, for example “Koppen er varm.”
